caption:
What do Koreans actually do for their skin every day?
Mostly ordinary things, done more often than you would expect.

Sun protection, but reapplied rather than upgraded. Water layered into the skin often and thinly, rather than loaded on once. And a lot of leaving it alone - fewer strong actives started at once, more of the same thing repeated.

None of that is Korean. The frequency is the local part.

The one part with numbers behind it is sunscreen. On Danish beaches, people applied roughly a quarter of the amount SPF is tested at. Asked to apply twice, the same people doubled what was on their skin and left much less of it uncovered. That is sun protection only, measured on bodies at a beach, with the SPF effect calculated rather than measured. The water and the leaving-alone parts are observation from practice, not a comparison between countries.

Which is also why it is worth copying. A better product is usually the smallest lever on this list. More steps is not the variable that moved. The same step done twice is the one that costs nothing.

The routine is not the point. The repetition is.

Heerfordt IM. Dan Med J 2018;65(4):B5476

General education only.

first_comment: The part that gets exported is the shelf, and the part that does the work does not photograph well. What is the one step you actually never skip?
